notes: Batch V (respiratory/nasal): budesonide-nebuliser, ipratropium, montelukast, mometasone-nasal, fluticasone-furoate-nasal, beclometasone-nasal. All have UK SmPCs on emc; none marked no-uk-product. budesonide-nebuliser also carries the clinic nasal spray (64 micrograms) as two formulations because the two UK nasal SmPCs differ: the prescription-only SmPC (emc-445) adds contraindications (haemostasis disorders, epistaxis, oro-nasal/ophthalmic herpes), says avoid breastfeeding during chronic treatment, licenses rhinitis from 6 years and lists French-style class interactions (aspirin, NSAIDs, fluoroquinolones, heparins, vitamin K antagonists, enzyme inducers, antacids); the pharmacy hay-fever SmPC (emc-10205) is adults only, max 3 months, breastfeeding may be considered. Both kept separately (formulation-scoped rules). beclometasone-nasal also carries the clinic 250 microgram inhaler. The clinic inhaler product has no UK SmPC (emc search found none); a different UK CFC-free 250 microgram pMDI SmPC (emc-6977) was used and flagged in the formulation note. brandPrescribing set for the inhaler only (MHRA DSU 2008 + SPS brand-name list); it does not apply to the nasal spray. Conflict (montelukast): the originator emc SmPC (emc-198, updated 15 Sep 2026) still says weigh risks/benefits of continuing if neuropsychiatric events occur, while the generic emc SmPC (emc-101340) and MHRA DSU April 2024 say discontinue montelukast if new or worsening neuropsychiatric symptoms occur. Both shown; MHRA advice used for stop criteria. The SmPC boxed warning that MHRA describes did not appear in the emc text of emc-198. Conflict (pregnancy/breastfeeding of nasal and inhaled steroids): several SmPCs say avoid / should not be used unless benefit outweighs risk (mometasone, beclometasone nasal and inhaler), while SPS (breastfeeding: all inhaled/intranasal corticosteroids compatible) and BUMPS/SPS (pregnancy: continue inhaled corticosteroids; intranasal corticosteroids can be considered) are more permissive. Rules keep the SmPC strength and quote SPS/BUMPS in the action. CYP3A wording kept as each SmPC states it: budesonide and mometasone SmPCs say CYP3A inhibitors (group:cyp3a4-inhibitor, avoid unless benefit outweighs risk; budesonide nasal SmPCs name clarithromycin); fluticasone furoate says potent CYP3A inhibitors (group:strong-cyp3a4-inhibitor, avoid; ritonavir not recommended - ritonavir is not in the master list); beclometasone says strong CYP3A inhibitors e.g. ritonavir, cobicistat (caution and monitoring). Group mapping caveats: montelukast inducer rule uses group:cyp3a4-inducer although the SmPC says inducers of CYP3A4, 2C8 and 2C9; budesonide nasal enzyme-inducer rule also uses group:cyp3a4-inducer. ipratropium beta2-agonist rule relies on beta2-agonist members being sourced by the inhaler batch. inhaled-corticosteroid membership is set at medicine level, so it also applies when only the nasal formulation of budesonide-nebuliser or beclometasone-nasal is used. Not found: no SPS breastfeeding page for montelukast or ipratropium; no SPS/BUMPS ipratropium-specific page; no UK renal/hepatic advice for ipratropium or mometasone. BNF not accessed (geo-blocked). | AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent check, see audit/V-W.md): budesonide-nebuliser, mometasone-nasal, fluticasone-furoate-nasal and beclometasone-nasal removed from group corticosteroid (local nasal products are never in systemic groups; inhaled products follow batch U, which keeps inhalers in inhaled-corticosteroid only). Nasal-spray rules that the SmPC states for other corticosteroids now have parallel inhaled-corticosteroid rules. budesonide aspirin rule removed: the SmPC limits it to analgesic/antipyretic doses (>=500 mg per dose) and the master-list aspirin is 75 mg only.
